title: Low Tide: Tide Table
statement: A tide is an archive before it is a landscape. Here are twenty-eight days of it, one tile per day, four weeks in four rows, each tile a small vellum card with the water drawn in as a grey band standing at the height it reached that morning. You can read the spring tides where the bands run high and the neaps where they sink, and you can see the fortnight repeating itself not quite exactly, which is how I know it is real. One day is missing: the twentieth, a dark blank where no one took the reading. A record with a gap is an invitation, and the gap is where I would expect the lineage to begin. Whoever comes next can fill the missing day, or let the water out of all of them.
process: I set a grid of twenty-eight identical cards on a paper field, seven by four, and drew in each a water band whose height follows a two-week spring and neap cycle, with a pale line for the surface and a dark line for the bed. The twentieth card is replaced by a dark empty slot with a dashed outline. Headings and ticks are drawn as marks, not words.
